aliases: Fe-Mn-Al-C low density steel without Zr

processing_steps.atmosphere: high vacuum (pressure below 10^-6 bar) then high-purity argon (pressure below 1 bar); remelted at least five times
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Raw materials (>99.8 wt% pure) placed in a water-cooled copper crucible; evacuated to below 10^-6 bar then high-purity Ar introduced; repeated melting at least five times to homogenize composition and reduce gas contamination. (Applies to all three Fe-Mn-Al-C steels.)
As-cast steels subjected to homogenization at 1200 °C for 2 h; Fig. S1 shows oxygen segregation to grain boundaries does not occur.
Hot-rolling with a thickness reduction of 40 %, followed by water quenching.
Hot-rolled plates subjected to cold rolling with an 80 % reduction.
Cold-rolled plates annealed at 900 °C for 5 min, followed by water-quenching; the Zr0 steel undergoes full recrystallization.

structures.overall_structure: Single-phase, homogeneous coarse-grained recrystallized FCC structure; the Zr0 steel annealed at 900 °C is fully recrystallized, consisting mainly of coarse recrystallized FCC grains.

defects.type: low dislocation density (uniformly low KAM, almost uniformly dark blue)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: unimodal; tallest fraction bar just above 0.15 at about 11 μm, small bars extending to ~23 μm

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: flat dog-bone-shaped samples with a gauge length of 14 mm and width of 4 mm, prepared from the cold-rolling plate along rolling direction (RD)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: uniaxial tensile testing using Instron 5892; data recorded via a contact extensometer

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve of Zr0 shown in Fig. 4a

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: prior to tensile deformation; 25 µm scale bar
characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal the microstructure of the Zr0 steel prior to tensile deformation
characterization_methods.key_findings: Equiaxed polygonal coarse FCC grains with a few isolated dark particles; matrix is single-phase coarse-grained FCC.

characterization_methods.technique: electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD): IPF, IQ and KAM maps
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SEM equipped with an EBSD detector (accelerating voltage: 30 kV, step size: 500 nm)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: prior to deformation; 40 µm scale bar
characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal the microstructure evolution of the Zr0 steel (grain orientation, quality and misorientation)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Equiaxed FCC grains with broad size distribution, random orientations and uniformly low KAM values.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Instron 5892 universal testing machine with contact extensometer
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature, strain rate 10^-3 s^-1, dog-bone specimen gauge length 14 mm, width 4 mm, along RD
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the room-temperature tensile properties of the Zr0 steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: Yield strength ~435 MPa, ultimate tensile strength 820 MPa, fracture ductility 52 %.

characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal the microscopic fracture morphology of the fractured Zr0 steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fracture surface mainly composed of small dimples and cleavage faces.

unmapped_findings: Nominal composition of the Zr0 steel is Fe-25Mn-7Al-0.9C-0Zr (wt.%); it is the Zr-free reference alloy used as baseline in the paper.
Average O content 12–89 ppm, N ~18 ppm and H ~2 ppm in the steelmaking process for these Fe-Mn-Al-C low density steels.

The Zr0 steel exhibits a homogeneous grain structure after the TMT treatment (contrasting with the heterogeneous grain structure developed in the Zr0.50 steel); increasing Zr content increases the FG zone fraction (0 % for Zr0).
The Zr0 steel's fracture surface consists mainly of small dimples and cleavage faces, in contrast to the larger, deeper and denser dimples of the higher-Zr steels.
